record.paper_title: Some open problems in the theory of topological groups and semigroups
record.original_question: Does there exist a Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group G, where paratopological means that the group multiplication map G x G -> G is continuous, that is not a topological group because the full topological-group continuity requirements fail?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A paratopological group is a group $G$ endowed with a topology such that the multiplication map $G\times G\to G$, $(x,y)\mapsto xy$, is jointly continuous (no continuity assumption is made on the inversion map $x\mapsto x^{-1}$). A paratopological group is a topological group if, in addition, inversion is continuous. Working in ZFC, decide the following question: does there exist a Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group whose inversion map is discontinuous (equivalently, a Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group that is not a topological group)?
artifact.status_search_result: Under additional set-theoretic assumptions (e.g., the existence of an infinite torsion-free abelian countably compact topological group without nontrivial convergent sequences), a functionally Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group that is not a topological group has been constructed (Banakh–Ravsky, "On feebly compact paratopological groups", arXiv:1003.5343). A ZFC example does not appear to be known, so the problem is partially solved (consistent example exists; ZFC status open).

status_evidence.title: On feebly compact paratopological groups
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of a functionally Hausdorff countably compact paratopological group that is not a topological group under the assumption of existence of an infinite torsion-free abelian countably compact topological group without non-trivial convergent sequences.
status_evidence.claim: A consistent example exists under a set-theoretic assumption beyond ZFC; no ZFC example is known.

status_evidence.title: On feebly compact paratopological groups - ScienceDirect
status_evidence.snippet: Studies necessary and sufficient conditions (such as quasiregularity) for a feebly compact paratopological group to be a topological group, constructing pathological examples otherwise.
status_evidence.claim: Related compact-like paratopological group examples have been constructed showing inversion can fail to be continuous.
